provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The input is a background of colour palette[8] with solid or hollow rectangular objects of colour palette[6]. The emitted program works directly on the visible grid and does two things, both read from the input. First, every 4-connected background component that does not touch the grid border is an enclosed hole, and it is painted palette[4]. Second, each 4-connected object component gets a one-cell ring of palette[3] just outside its bounding box. The ring is clipped to the grid and painted only on cells that are still background, so overlapping rings simply merge. Both steps are invariant under D4: rotating or reflecting the grid preserves enclosed components and bounding-box rings. So d4 needs no axis or direction specialization, and only the four colour roles are fixed as palette constants.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the generator's domain: objects are axis-aligned rectangles separated by gaps of at least 2 cells, so rings never cover object cells and no background pocket forms between different objects. Each hole is strictly interior to its rectangle. Background and object colours are taken from palette[8] and palette[6] rather than inferred from the demonstrations. The demonstrations are not used. No fixture contradictions were found. I have not run any tests.
